title: Pillar 2: The Mole Concept & Chemical Calculations
subject: chem

questions.questionText: Calculate the relative formula mass ($M_r$) of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$. [Relative atomic masses: $Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1$]

solution.commonTrap: Multiplying $160 \times 90$ because of the 'dot' symbol instead of adding.

questions.questionText: How many moles of gas are present in $6.0\text{ dm}^3$ of oxygen gas ($O_2$) measured at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.)? [Molar volume at r.t.p. $= 24\text{ dm}^3/\text{mol}$]

solution.formulaSetup: Number of moles $n = \frac{\text{Volume in dm}^3}{\text{Molar volume at r.t.p.}} = \frac{V}{24}$
solution.commonTrap: Multiplying $6 \times 24 = 144\text{ mol}$ or dividing by 32 ($M_r$) instead of molar gas volume.

questions.questionText: What is the mass of $0.40\text{ mol}$ of calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$)? [$A_r$: $Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16$]

solution.formulaSetup: Mass $m = n \times M_r$.
solution.commonTrap: Dividing $0.40 / 100$ or arithmetic error computing $M_r$.

questions.questionText: Find the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate ($NH_4NO_3$). [$A_r$: $N = 14, H = 1, O = 16$]

solution.formulaSetup: $\text{Percentage by mass} = \frac{2 \times A_r(N)}{M_r(NH_4NO_3)} \times 100\%$.
steps: Count nitrogen atoms: 2 nitrogen atoms per formula unit ($NH_4$ and $NO_3$).
solution.commonTrap: Only counting one nitrogen atom ($14/80 = 17.5\%$).

questions.questionText: Calculate the concentration in $\text{mol/dm}^3$ of a solution prepared by dissolving $10.6\text{ g}$ of sodium carbonate ($Na_2CO_3$, $M_r = 106$) in distilled water to make $250\text{ cm}^3$ of solution.

solution.formulaSetup: Moles $n = \frac{m}{M_r}$, Concentration $C = \frac{n}{V(\text{in dm}^3)}$.
solution.commonTrap: Forgetting to divide $250\text{ cm}^3$ by $1000$, resulting in $0.0004\text{ mol/dm}^3$.

questions.questionText: A compound contains $40\%$ carbon, $6.7\%$ hydrogen, and $53.3\%$ oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? [$A_r$: $C = 12, H = 1, O = 16$]

solution.formulaSetup: Convert mass percentages to mole ratios: $n = \frac{\%}{A_r}$.
solution.commonTrap: Confusing molecular formula ($C_2H_4O_2$) with empirical formula ($CH_2O$).

questions.questionText: Consider the reaction: $2Al + 3Cl_2 \to 2AlCl_3$. If $5.4\text{ g}$ of aluminium is reacted with $28.4\text{ g}$ of chlorine gas, which is the limiting reactant, and what mass of $AlCl_3$ is produced? [$A_r$: $Al = 27, Cl = 35.5$]

solution.formulaSetup: Calculate moles of each reactant and compare with stoichiometric ratio $2Al : 3Cl_2$.
steps: Stoichiometry: $0.20\text{ mol}$ of $Al$ requires $\frac{3}{2} \times 0.20 = 0.30\text{ mol}$ of $Cl_2$.
Since $0.40\text{ mol}$ of $Cl_2$ is available ($0.40 > 0.30$), $Cl_2$ is in excess and $Al$ is the LIMITING reactant.
Moles of $AlCl_3$ produced = Moles of $Al = 0.20\text{ mol}$.
solution.commonTrap: Choosing $Cl_2$ as limiting because $28.4\text{ g}$ looks closer or forgetting that chlorine gas is diatomic ($Cl_2, M_r = 71$).

questions.questionText: What volume of carbon dioxide gas, measured at r.t.p., is produced when $5.0\text{ g}$ of calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$, $M_r = 100$) reacts completely with excess hydrochloric acid? [$CaCO_3 + 2HCl \to CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2$]

solution.formulaSetup: $n(CaCO_3) = \frac{m}{M_r}$. From balanced equation, $n(CO_2) = n(CaCO_3)$. Volume $V = n \times 24\text{ dm}^3$.
steps: Mole ratio: $1\text{ mol } CaCO_3 \to 1\text{ mol } CO_2$, so $n(CO_2) = 0.050\text{ mol}$
solution.commonTrap: Dividing by 2 because of the coefficient 2 in $2HCl$, which applies to the acid, not $CO_2$.

questions.questionText: In a titration, $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.150\text{ mol/dm}^3$ sodium hydroxide solution ($NaOH$) required $18.75\text{ cm}^3$ of sulfuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) for complete neutralisation. Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid. [$2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \to Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O$]

solution.formulaSetup: $n(NaOH) = C_b V_b$. From mole ratio, $n(H_2SO_4) = \frac{1}{2} n(NaOH)$. $C_a = \frac{n(H_2SO_4)}{V_a}$.
steps: From balanced equation, 2 moles of $NaOH$ react with 1 mole of $H_2SO_4$:
solution.commonTrap: Forgetting the $2:1$ mole ratio and assuming $1:1$ neutralisation, which gives an incorrect concentration of $0.200\text{ mol/dm}^3$.

questions.questionText: Heating $4.92\text{ g}$ of hydrated magnesium sulfate ($MgSO_4 \cdot xH_2O$) drove off all water of crystallisation, leaving $2.40\text{ g}$ of anhydrous $MgSO_4$ ($M_r = 120$). Find the value of $x$. [$M_r(H_2O) = 18$]

solution.formulaSetup: Mass of water lost = Total mass - Anhydrous mass. Mole ratio $x = \frac{n(H_2O)}{n(MgSO_4)}$.
solution.commonTrap: Dividing initial hydrated mass $4.92\text{ g}$ by $120$ instead of using the anhydrous mass.

questions.questionText: In an experiment, $12.0\text{ g}$ of iron(III) oxide was reduced by carbon monoxide: $Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \to 2Fe + 3CO_2$. If $6.30\text{ g}$ of iron was obtained, calculate the percentage yield. [$M_r(Fe_2O_3) = 160, A_r(Fe) = 56$]

solution.formulaSetup: $\text{Percentage Yield} = \frac{\text{Actual Yield}}{\text{Theoretical Yield}} \times 100\%$.
solution.commonTrap: Dividing actual mass ($6.30\text{ g}$) directly by the mass of reactant ($12.0\text{ g}$), giving $52.5\%$.

questions.questionText: An impure sample of limestone of mass $2.50\text{ g}$ containing $CaCO_3$ ($M_r = 100$) was reacted with excess hydrochloric acid. It generated $0.540\text{ dm}^3$ of carbon dioxide gas at r.t.p. What is the percentage purity of $CaCO_3$ in the limestone?

solution.formulaSetup: $n(CO_2) = \frac{V}{24}$. $n(CaCO_3) = n(CO_2)$. $\text{Purity} = \frac{\text{pure mass}}{\text{sample mass}} \times 100\%$.
steps: From $CaCO_3 + 2HCl \to CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2$, moles of pure $CaCO_3 = 0.0225\text{ mol}$.
solution.commonTrap: Rounding $0.0225$ prematurely to $0.02$, resulting in an inaccurate purity percentage.

questions.questionText: What volume of oxygen gas at r.t.p. is required for the complete combustion of $15\text{ dm}^3$ of propane gas ($C_3H_8$) at the same temperature and pressure? [$C_3H_8 + 5O_2 \to 3CO_2 + 4H_2O$]

solution.formulaSetup: Avogadro's Law: Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of moles. Volume ratio = Mole ratio.
steps: Examine stoichiometric coefficients of gases: $1\text{ volume } C_3H_8 : 5\text{ volumes } O_2$.
solution.commonTrap: Converting unnecessarily to moles via 24 and making arithmetic errors instead of using direct volume ratios.

questions.questionText: A hydrocarbon $Q$ contains $85.7\%$ carbon and $14.3\%$ hydrogen by mass. Given that $1.40\text{ g}$ of $Q$ occupies $0.60\text{ dm}^3$ at r.t.p., find its molecular formula. [$A_r$: $C = 12, H = 1$]

solution.formulaSetup: Step 1: Find empirical formula. Step 2: Calculate $M_r$ using $n = \frac{V}{24}$ and $M_r = \frac{m}{n}$. Step 3: Molecular formula $= (\text{Empirical})_k$.
steps: Ratio: $C : H = 1 : 2 \implies$ Empirical formula is $CH_2$ (Empirical mass $= 14$).
solution.commonTrap: Choosing $C_2H_4$ ($M_r = 28$) or $C_3H_6$ ($M_r = 42$) due to inverted mole calculation.

questions.questionText: A mixture of methane ($CH_4$) and ethane ($C_2H_6$) of total volume $20\text{ cm}^3$ requires $55\text{ cm}^3$ of oxygen for complete combustion at r.t.p. Determine the volume of ethane in the mixture.

solution.formulaSetup: Combustion equations: (1) $CH_4 + 2O_2 \to CO_2 + 2H_2O$; (2) $C_2H_6 + 3.5O_2 \to 2CO_2 + 3H_2O$.
steps: Let volume of $CH_4 = x\text{ cm}^3$ and volume of $C_2H_6 = y\text{ cm}^3$.
If total oxygen is $55\text{ cm}^3$, then $1.5y = 15 \implies y = 10\text{ cm}^3$! Let's update oxygen volume in question to $55\text{ cm}^3$!
solution.commonTrap: Using $3O_2$ instead of $3.5O_2$ for ethane combustion.

questions.questionText: A sample of $1.50\text{ g}$ of an alloy containing copper and aluminium was treated with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. Only the aluminium reacted, producing $1.20\text{ dm}^3$ of hydrogen gas at r.t.p. Calculate the percentage by mass of copper in the alloy. [$2Al + 6HCl \to 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2$, $A_r(Al) = 27$]

solution.formulaSetup: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series and does NOT react with dilute $HCl$. Only $Al$ reacts: $2Al \leftrightarrow 3H_2$.
steps: From stoichiometry, moles of $Al = \frac{2}{3} \times n(H_2) = \frac{2}{3} \times 0.050 = \frac{0.100}{3} = 0.03333\text{ mol}$.
Mass of copper in alloy = Total mass - Mass of $Al = 1.50 - 0.900 = 0.600\text{ g}$.
solution.commonTrap: Calculating the percentage of aluminium ($60.0\%$) instead of copper, or assuming copper reacts with $HCl$.

questions.questionText: In a back titration, $50.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $1.00\text{ mol/dm}^3$ hydrochloric acid was added to $2.00\text{ g}$ of an impure sample of calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$, $M_r = 100$). The unreacted excess acid required $16.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $1.00\text{ mol/dm}^3$ sodium hydroxide for neutralisation. Find the percentage purity of the calcium carbonate.

solution.formulaSetup: Back titration principle: $\text{Moles of acid reacted with } CaCO_3 = \text{Total acid added} - \text{Excess acid neutralised by } NaOH$.
steps: Since $HCl + NaOH \to NaCl + H_2O$, moles of unreacted excess $HCl = 0.0160\text{ mol}$.
Moles of $HCl$ that reacted with $CaCO_3 = 0.0500 - 0.0160 = 0.0340\text{ mol}$.
solution.commonTrap: Forgetting to divide by 2 for the $2:1$ mole ratio between $HCl$ and $CaCO_3$.

questions.questionText: When $0.200\text{ mol}$ of an unknown metal $M$ reacted with excess dilute sulfuric acid, $4.80\text{ dm}^3$ of hydrogen gas was produced at r.t.p. What is the charge of the metal cation formed in this reaction?

solution.formulaSetup: Let the reaction be $M + \frac{n}{2}H_2SO_4 \to M(SO_4)_{n/2} + \frac{n}{2}H_2$ where $n$ is the charge of $M^{n+}$.
steps: A $1:1$ ratio corresponds to: $M + H_2SO_4 \to MSO_4 + H_2$.
In $MSO_4$, the sulfate ion has a charge of $-2$, which means the metal cation is $M^{2+}$ (charge $+2$).
solution.commonTrap: Assuming the ratio is always $2:3$ like aluminium.

questions.questionText: A solution of $100\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.500\text{ mol/dm}^3$ silver nitrate ($AgNO_3$) is mixed with $100\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.300\text{ mol/dm}^3$ barium chloride ($BaCl_2$). Find the mass of the precipitate formed. [$AgNO_3 + BaCl_2 \to AgCl(s) + \dots$, $M_r(AgCl) = 143.5$]

solution.formulaSetup: Net ionic equation: $Ag^+(aq) + Cl^-(aq) \to AgCl(s)$. Determine the limiting ion.
steps: Since each formula unit of $BaCl_2$ yields $2Cl^-$ ions: moles of $Cl^- = 2 \times 0.0300 = 0.0600\text{ mol}$.
Compare moles: $0.0500\text{ mol } Ag^+$ vs $0.0600\text{ mol } Cl^-$.
solution.commonTrap: Forgetting that $BaCl_2$ provides $2$ moles of $Cl^-$ per mole of salt, mistaking $BaCl_2$ for the limiting reagent.

questions.questionText: An organic compound contains carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen only. Complete combustion of $0.220\text{ g}$ of the compound yielded $0.440\text{ g}$ of $CO_2$ and $0.180\text{ g}$ of $H_2O$. Find the empirical formula of the compound. [$A_r$: $C = 12, H = 1, O = 16$]

solution.formulaSetup: Determine masses of $C$ and $H$ from combustion products. Mass of $O = \text{Total} - m(C) - m(H)$.
steps: Mass of $C = \frac{12}{44} \times 0.440 = 0.120\text{ g}$. Moles of $C = \frac{0.120}{12} = 0.010\text{ mol}$.
Mass of $H = \frac{2}{18} \times 0.180 = 0.020\text{ g}$. Moles of $H = \frac{0.020}{1} = 0.020\text{ mol}$.
solution.commonTrap: Assuming all oxygen in $CO_2$ and $H_2O$ came from the compound, forgetting that atmospheric $O_2$ was added during combustion.
